title: Choose the AidOS visual world
question: The roll assigned the Status Rack: the T-card board incident command centres use to track resources. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Status Rack
options.lineage: Incident Command System T-card resource racks
options.thesis: Every unit of stock is a card in a slot, so the depot, each zone and every state is a column you can read at a glance.
options.viewport: A slate rack: a condensed signage headline, then depot and zone columns of resource cards showing stock against requests, with shortfalls tabbed in amber.
options.risk: Reads as an operations-room costume if the rack becomes ornament instead of holding real scenario data.

raised.raise: Every element states its epistemic status (implemented, planned, synthetic) as a visible typographic distinction, never hidden in footnotes.
Colour lives only on state that matters (shortfall, critical, selected lane); at rest the rack stays in card-stock neutrals.
The hero rack demonstrates the mechanism on its own: picking a resource lane isolates it across depot and zones.
The dashboard summary has a fixed cross-check reading order (stock, requests, shortfall, status), each tile owning one truth.
The headline is set at commanding scale against small tracked labels; no timid mid-size hero type.

options.label: Isotype Count
options.thesis: Supplies are counted as rows of repeated unit symbols, so scarcity shows as dashed symbols nobody can fill.
options.viewport: A geometric headline over rows of unit symbols: stock in solid teal, unmet requests as dashed outlines.
options.risk: Familiar: Isotype-style infographics are where many data-explainer pages land, and pictograms can read as charity marketing.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Supply flows traced as one ribbon splitting from depot into zones.
options.viewport: A ribbon leaving the depot and splitting into zone branches.
options.risk: Archival buff and serif ledgers drift into the cream-and-serif default.
options.case: Fuses weakly: coordinators and markers do not see themselves in museum custody records.
options.kept: Known versus inferred versus disputed, written into the type.

options.label: Plankton Wake
options.thesis: Scenario changes light up as wakes on a dark field.
options.viewport: A dark field where pointer motion traces glowing wakes.
options.risk: Neon on black breaks the calm, auditable brief.
options.case: Fuses poorly: decorative motion hides the numbers markers must audit.
options.kept: Only active state carries light; everything at rest goes quiet.

options.label: Arcade Marquee Row
options.thesis: Each policy as a cabinet with an attract-mode preview.
options.viewport: A dark aisle of glowing policy cabinets.
options.risk: Gamifies a humanitarian subject, which the spec forbids.
options.case: Fails the brand: gamified catastrophe is explicitly out.
options.kept: The attract loop: the product demonstrates itself before you commit.

options.label: Signboard Canyon
options.thesis: Zones stacked as lit floor signs, illumination as status.
options.viewport: A vertical spine of lit zone signs.
options.risk: Nightlife atmosphere is far from the emergency-ops context.
options.case: Fuses poorly on audience; status-as-illumination is the only transfer.
options.kept: One voice per destination, stacked into an index.

options.label: Night Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six gauges, each owning one truth, read in a cross-check sweep.
options.viewport: Two rows of three round gauges for stock, demand and shortfall.
options.risk: An instrument costume on a data screen; gauges hide exact integers.
options.case: Holds clarity partly but loses audience fit and integer auditability.
options.kept: A fixed cross-check reading order for the summary metrics.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: A breathing shader field with thin type floating over it.
options.viewport: Full-screen shader with one oversized word.
options.risk: Decorative GPU motion with nothing to audit; heavy on lab laptops.
options.case: Loses both axes: says nothing about allocation.
options.kept: Commanding display scale against tiny margin labels.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A navy SaaS landing page: headline left, dashboard screenshot right, feature cards below.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero with copy beside a dashboard mock, then a row of feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other analytics product by design.
